lines.en: Hi Omar! You look annoyed. What happened?
Hi Sara. I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with a laptop I bought last month. It broke after two weeks.
Not only was the product damaged, but I bet the service was slow too.
Exactly. It was not until I threatened to contact consumer protection that the company finally responded.
What I find particularly disappointing is how companies treat customers after the sale.
Anyway, they offered me a small discount on a new one. Now comes the hard part: negotiation.
What every skilled negotiator knows is that listening is more powerful than speaking.
True. And however tempting it may be to win every point, a good negotiator knows when to compromise.
Not until both sides feel they have gained something is a deal truly successful.
Enough about shops. Did I tell you about the nature reserve I visited on Friday?
No! What makes the desert so remarkable is the variety of life that survives there, right?
Absolutely. Not until the reserve was established did the number of gazelles begin to recover.
Little do we realize how deeply every creature is connected to the balance of its environment.
The guide told us it is not the strongest species that survives, but the one most able to adapt.
Speaking of survival, have you seen the prices this week?
Unfortunately. What worries economists is not the debt itself, but the speed at which it is growing.
However strong a currency may seem, it rests on nothing but the trust of those who use it.
It is not wealth that makes a country stable, but the fairness with which that wealth is shared.
The price of bread is said to affect political stability more than any election speech.
Heavy topics today. But that reminds me of a question I wanted to ask you.
Go ahead.
If your friend did something wrong at work, would you tell the manager, or protect your friend?
That is a real dilemma. What makes a dilemma a dilemma is that every choice carries a cost someone must pay.
However good our intentions may be, what matters in the end is the effect of our actions.
It is said that character is what you do when nobody is watching.
Rarely is the easiest choice also the right one.
I think I would tell my friend first, and give them the chance to fix it themselves.
That sounds fair. What we owe others is honesty, even when it is uncomfortable.
Agreed. Now, go finish that complaint letter before the shop closes!
Little does the shop manager know what is coming. See you tomorrow, Sara!
